goal: Add the cmux `browser` verb family to cmuxctl.mjs behind a frozen sub-verb allowlist, with six bounded wrappers and code-only error logging, plus full fake-cmux fixture fidelity for the family — the foundation slice of issue #12 (4b browser preview singleton, PR 1 of 2, plugin 0.1.63 at be-12-02).
constraints: scripts/cmux/contract.mjs must be byte-identical (ADR-013 freeze) — do not touch it, do not import from it anew.

The normative design is .claude/dev-team/tasks/issue-12/architecture-package-v2.md WITH the v2.1 errata appended at its end — where the errata (sections E1-E11) contradicts the v2 body, THE ERRATA WINS. For this slice the errata changes browserOpen's signature (E1), keeps closeSurface unchanged (E2), and moves browserErrorsList's 10000ms bound into the IC-2 block (E9).

BROWSER_SUBVERBS = Object.freeze(['open','goto','wait','errors','screenshot']) — module-private frozen constant; browserVerb(sub, args, opts) throws BEFORE any spawn on a sub-verb outside it. eval, state, console, snapshot, viewport and every interaction verb must be structurally unreachable.

browser never enters VERB_METHODS. Add a comment at the VERB_METHODS definition site (cmuxctl.mjs:58-63) stating WHY, in the existing decision-not-omission voice: the map is one-verb-to-one-RPC-method and cannot represent a five-method family, and the preview is non-load-bearing so it degrades rather than hard-stops preflight.

Every wrapper passes an explicit timeoutMs (values in interface_contract) exceeding any cmux-side --timeout-ms, so a spawn kill (spawn_error) stays distinguishable from cmux's own bound (js_error / navigation_timeout).

Error logging is CODE-ONLY: wrappers log res.error?.code + the sub-verb + the surface id, NEVER res.error?.message (browser error details are page-influenced; dispatch.mjs stderr is an orchestrator-context ingress). The code is logged only if it matches ^[a-z_]{1,32}$, else the literal <unparsed>. State the deliberate divergence from the house `err.message` pattern in a comment at the definition site.

Wrappers degrade loudly (one stderr line, null/false return) and never throw on a cmux failure — the setStatus/readScreen shape. They throw before any spawn on a missing/malformed id (the setPhase shape, conventions.md 2026-08-06).

browserOpen parses ONLY placement=(\w+) from stdout — never the surface=/pane= tokens, not even as a cross-check (they are positional refs; JSDoc: placement is log-only, never persisted, never branched on). Id recovery per errata E1: the caller supplies treeBefore (its own scan tree); browserOpen issues the open, takes exactly ONE bounded tree read (timeoutMs 3000) as treeAfter, runs recoverNewId(treeBefore, treeAfter, ...), and returns treeAfter to the caller. Two tree spawns per create TOTAL across caller+wrapper — browserOpen contributes exactly one.
BROWSER_LOAD_STATE = 'complete' is a frozen module constant; no caller supplies a load state; the literal 'load' must appear nowhere in scripts/cmux/.
tree() gains an OPTIONAL timeoutMs parameter, default undefined = today's behavior byte-for-byte at every existing call site.
closeSurface is unchanged — no opts parameter is added (errata E2/E11).
--focus false on browserOpen's argv; no browser wrapper ever issues a focus verb.

Fixture doctrine: hostile/degraded cases are pre-seeded _simulate* state flags in FAKE_CMUX_STATE, NEVER new env switches (fake-cmux.mjs:401,:495 precedent). Frozen live captures for every output shape (see discovery_context). Unknown browser sub-verb in the fixture → fail('bad_args', ...).

Test doctrine: positives first (the E-P1 anti-vacuity shape at test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs:8-13,172-219); argv asserted element-by-element with exact invocation counts; new browser tests live IN test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs (a new test file cannot reuse setUpWorkspace/freshCmuxEnv — importing a test file re-registers its whole suite, backend-notes 2026-08-01).

Updating test/cmux-preflight.test.mjs:242-255's unverifiable_verbs deepEqual is an EXPECTED red from adding browser to VERBS — update it in this slice; also mirror the existing comment style there explaining why browser lands in the unverifiable set.
No version bump in this slice (0.1.63 lands at be-12-02, the PR-1 tip).
acceptance_criteria: VERBS contains 'browser'; runVerb still refuses anything outside VERBS before spawning; test/cmux-contract.test.mjs and test/cmux-preflight.test.mjs pass with the updated unverifiable_verbs expectation.
An out-of-allowlist sub-verb (e.g. 'eval', 'state') throws before any spawn — zero entries in the fixture invocation log.

Each of the six wrappers has a positives-first happy-path test with argv asserted element-by-element and exact counts, including --focus false on browserOpen and --load-state complete + --timeout-ms 20000 on browserWaitReady.
The literal 'load' appears nowhere in scripts/cmux/ (source-text assertion); BROWSER_LOAD_STATE is the single definition site of 'complete'.

Each wrapper's argv/spawn carries its exact timeoutMs from the interface contract, asserted per wrapper; a hang test per bounded call (fixture _simulateTreeHang / _simulateBrowserOpenHang, Atomics.wait per the FAKE_CMUX_EVENTS_HANG precedent at fake-cmux.mjs:610-618) proves it returns with code spawn_error within its bound.

Each wrapper throws before spawn on a missing id with zero logged invocations; a js_error or navigation_timeout from the fixture degrades to null/false without throwing, logging exactly one stderr line containing the error CODE and NOT the detail string (assert the detail is absent from captured stderr); an out-of-vocabulary code logs <unparsed>.
Return-type assertions for all six wrappers: boolean / {surfaceId,paneId,placement,treeAfter} / null only — browserErrorsList is the sole wrapper returning a string.
browserOpen under _simulateConcurrentCreate (fake-cmux.mjs:401) surfaces the recoverNewId ambiguity rather than guessing.

Fixture fidelity: open prints 'OK surface=surface:<n> pane=pane:<n> placement=split' with POSITIONAL refs (an implementation parsing the printed id produces a non-UUID and fails); a second open into a workspace holding a browser surface prints placement=reuse and STACKS a second surface into that pane; wait/errors on any surface in a pane holding >=2 browser-typed surfaces fail('js_error','Timed out waiting for the browser document to become ready') while screenshot there still succeeds and writes a file; --load-state rejects 'load' (only interactive|complete succeed); browser surface title tracks the URL hostname (set on open, updated on goto); rename-tab fails 'not_found','Tab not found' when the target surface type !== 'terminal'; navigation_timeout is modeled alongside js_error; _simulateScreenshotOkNoWrite prints 'OK <path>' WITHOUT writing the file.

Mutations that must go red (verify by applying each, observing the failure, then reverting): remove the BROWSER_SUBVERBS guard; remove any wrapper's timeoutMs; restore err.message logging in a browser wrapper.

interface_contract:
IC-2 (v2 §4 as amended by errata E1 + E9) — produced by THIS slice, consumed by be-12-02/be-12-03:

BROWSER_SUBVERBS = ['open','goto','wait','errors','screenshot']  // frozen, module-private
BROWSER_LOAD_STATE = 'complete'  // frozen export; 'load' is invalid on 0.64.22

browserOpen(url, { workspaceId, treeBefore }) -> { surfaceId, paneId, placement, treeAfter } | null   // spawn timeoutMs 5000 for the open; its single own tree read bounded at 3000; --focus false; placement log-only
browserGoto(surfaceId, url) -> boolean            // 20000 (cmux self-bounds ~15.5s -> navigation_timeout)
browserWaitReady(surfaceId, { timeoutMs } = {}) -> boolean   // spawn 25000 over cmux-side --load-state complete --timeout-ms 20000
browserErrorsClear(surfaceId) -> boolean          // 10000
browserErrorsList(surfaceId) -> string | null     // 10000; RAW page bytes; sole legal consumer is be-12-03's reduceBrowserErrors; never logs its payload
browserScreenshot(surfaceId, outPath) -> boolean  // 20000; caller confirms via existsSync, never the OK line

tree({ all, timeoutMs }) — timeoutMs optional, default undefined (unchanged behavior everywhere today).
All wrappers: throw before spawn on missing/malformed id; degrade loudly (code-only stderr line, null/false) on cmux failure; never throw on non-zero exit; treeBefore is supplied by the caller and treeAfter returned to it — browserOpen is the only wrapper that takes or returns a tree, and the coupling is deliberate (it is what makes be-12-02's 11s lock budget true). Return types are contract: only browserErrorsList returns a string.
